notes.decision: Translated 'the foremost Darkness which reigned over him.' ⲛⲧⲍⲟⲩⲓⲧⲉ = ⲛ̄-ⲧ-ϣⲟⲣⲡ 'of the foremost' (Lyc. ⲍⲟⲩⲓⲧ in vocab); ⲛⲧⲁϩⲟⲣⲟ = relative perfect 'which reigned' (cf. accumulated ⲛ̄ϩⲟⲣⲟ ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ 'reign over').
Marked break_after=true. Mid-discourse paragraph break in the new chapter, possibly between disciples' question and Mani's response.

Translated 'the Greatness of the Light is with one another forever.' This is the kephalaion's opening principle: in the realm of Light, the great ones (or the manifestations of Greatness) coexist harmoniously. The line picks up syntactically from the previous page; ⲙⲛ ⲛⲟⲩⲉⲣⲏⲩ 'with one another' establishes the cooperative ontology that contrasts with Darkness's solitary self-existence in the lines that follow.

Translated 'reaped' from ⲱⲱⲥ/ⲟⲩⲱⲥϩ 'reap, cut down' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲱⲉⲥ 'to reap,' ⲟⲩⲱⲥϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'cut away from'). The doublet 'appointed and reaped' describes the cosmic action against the enemy. Alternative reading 'answered' (ⲟⲩⲱⲥⲃ) is possible but less idiomatic in this context.

Read 'he is one of (a single) practice in the principle, he himself alone.' ⲡⲣⲁⲭ = πρᾶξις 'practice'; ϩⲡⲁⲣⲝ̄ tentatively read as ϩⲛ̄-(ⲁ)ⲣⲭⲏ 'in the principle/beginning' or possibly ὕπαρξις 'existence.' ⲁⲭⲱϩ ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲉⲧϩ is the intensive reflexive 'he himself alone' (cf. fem. ⲁⲭⲱⲥ ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲉⲧⲥ̄ in next line). The sense: each kingdom — Darkness and Light — is self-enclosed in its own mode of being.

Translated 'they do honor to her' tentatively. The verb ⲣⲱϣⲧⲏⲣⲉ is unattested elsewhere; possibly compound ⲣ̄-ⲱϣⲧ-ⲧⲏⲣⲉ 'do-honor-wholly,' or related to ⲱϣⲧ̄ 'worship.' Alternative readings: 'are wholly content with her' (from ⲣⲱϣⲉ 'suffice'). Flag for parallels.

Read as a verb of separation/transgression 'against her,' parallel to ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲃⲁ in line 2. The editor's restored stem [ⲡⲁⲣⲭ] could be Greek παράγω 'lead astray' or a reduced form of ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲃⲁ or ⲡⲱⲣⲭ 'separate.' ⲁⲭⲱⲥ here functions as suffixal directional 'against her.' Translation tentative.

Standard formula 'according to this comparison, you yourselves' marks the transition from cosmic to paraenetic register. The teacher applies the cosmic principle (united Light vs. isolated Darkness) directly to the disciples' communal life: agreement, single-heartedness, and adherence to revealed truth produce the same overcoming-power that Light has over Darkness.
Greek loan ὦ μὴ γένοιτο 'O may it not happen!' — a parenthetical optative-apotropaic standard in Greek diatribe. The teacher inserts it to ward off even hypothetical apostasy.
